title: Social Cohesion through Common Spaces in Residential Estates
what_it_is: Social Cohesion through Common Spaces in Residential Estates

sections.label: Social cohesion and COVID-19 outcomes
sections.summary: Societies with greater social cohesion have had better COVID-19 outcomes and can overcome disasters, terrorism and national crisis.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Societies with greater social cohesion and cohesiveness have been shown to have had better outcomes from COVID-19 and the same can be said with such societies in overcoming disasters, acts of terrorism and bouncing back from national crisis.

sections.label: Closure of common spaces
sections.summary: There has been news coverage, opinion pieces and debate over closures of common spaces in residential estates in Woodlands and Bedok North.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In recent months, there have been news coverage, opinion pieces and debate over the closure of some common spaces in residential estates, specifically, a barricaded void deck in Woodlands Ring Road and the closure of a football hard court in Bedok North Road.

sections.label: Concerns over closing common areas
sections.summary: The speaker understands Town Councils' challenges but offers three areas of concern on social cohesion over closing common areas.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I can understand the challenges of Town Councils in moderating complaints and disagreements on the ground.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, when we take steps to close common areas of play or restrict areas of spontaneity from fair and legitimate interests like sports, for example, I offer three areas of concern relating to social cohesion for the House to consider and ponder upon.

sections.label: Play in residential common spaces
sections.summary: Strengthening social cohesion requires finding ways to allow reasonable play and activity in common spaces of residential estates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For us to strengthen our social cohesion, we must find ways and means to allow for reasonable play and activity within the common spaces of our residential estates.

sections.label: Designing estates for social cohesion
sections.summary: If social cohesion and community space activities are key outcomes, challenges should be eliminated by design in new and existing estates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At the outset, if, indeed, social cohesion and community space activities are key intended outcomes of residential living, we should endeavour to eliminate most challenges proximally by design.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If safety of passers-by is to be considered, can we not demarcate and design areas of play better?

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I believe it is not impossible for both new and existing estates to be adapted to foster such activities if we resolve together that social cohesion is an important area we want to develop and further strengthen in our people.

sections.label: HDB Solar Nova Programme
sections.summary: Under the Solar Nova Programme, HDB has endeavoured to install solar panels on more than 8,000 blocks over the past decade.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Under the Solar Nova Programme, into its eighth leasing tender last year, HDB has endeavoured to install more than 8,000 blocks with solar panels over the past decade.

sections.label: Co-creating common spaces in estates
sections.summary: The Motion addresses co-creating and curating common spaces in residential estates to foster understanding and interaction among Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Motion speaks to how we can and must co-create and curate the common spaces in residential estates, to foster better understanding amongst Singaporeans and consciously allow for the opportunity to interact in a manner that transcends our layered identities and interests.

sections.label: Planning urban spaces and last-mile delivery
sections.summary: Urban living spaces are planned with multicultural and interethnic balance, but last-mile delivery and policy integrate social cohesion work.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We take careful thought in the planning of our urban living spaces and we have done well, over decades, to ensure there is a good balance multicultural representation and interethnic presence in our residential estates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would argue, though, that it is in the last mile delivery and policy – the one that fronts the experience of the ordinary Singaporean – that integrates and converges all the proximal work that is done for social cohesion.

sections.label: HDB activities and resident outreach
sections.summary: HDB hosts about 600 activities and events yearly reaching 220,000 residents at town plazas with various partners.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Each year, HDB hosts some 600 activities and events with an outreach of 220,000 residents at town plazas, in collaboration with agencies, such as SportSG, National Arts Council and Health Promotion Board, as well as schools and grassroots organisations.

sections.label: Lively Places Programme disbursements
sections.summary: As of end-2023, over $1.1 million was disbursed and committed under the Lively Places Programme, supporting 229 projects.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: As of end-2023, we have disbursed and committed more than $1.1 million under the Lively Places Programme, supporting 229 projects that enliven common spaces and strengthen community identity.

sections.label: Remaking Our Heartland community design
sections.summary: Under the third Remaking Our Heartland run, HDB worked with close to 6,000 residents and stakeholders on community nodes, parks and playgrounds.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Under the third run of the Remaking Our Heartland Programme, HDB worked with close to 6,000 residents and community stakeholders for the design of six community nodes, 10 neighbourhood parks and four Build-A-Playground projects in Toa Payoh, Woodlands and Pasir Ris.

sections.label: Town Councils managing common spaces
sections.summary: Town Councils manage common spaces in public housing estates, with residents applying for permission, ensuring fairness and efficient use given land constraints.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Today, our Town Councils manage and maintain the common spaces in public housing estates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Residents who wish to use the common spaces are required to apply to the Town Councils for permission.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We note the Member's concerns that such arrangements may not be ideal to some residents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: However, given Singapore's land constraints, we need to ensure fairness and efficient use of space in our housing estates, while creating a conducive and harmonious living environment.
